text.content:
The Lord of Mad Mansion

Level 4-5 Mystery Puzzle Mansion

Designed by: Sticky

Playtest: RED1, Mellow, Potato

Made for: 2024 ShadowDark Weird Tales Game Jam

Cover Art: Margaret Brundage

Cartography: Dyson Logos

Inspiration: The Man Who Loved Planks by Malcolm Jameson, published in Weird Tales (March 1941)

LICENSE

The Lord of Mad Mansion is an independent product published under the Shadowdark RPG Third-Party License and is not affiliated with The Arcane Library, LLC. Shadowdark RPG (c) 2023 The Arcane Library, LLC.

The Man Who Loved Planks Synopsis

The Lord of Mad Mansion, Enoch Warren, has been found dead cradling a plank of wood in his arms. He's depicted as an eccentric, middle-aged man with an intense, peculiar obsession with collecting furniture and wooden planks. This fixation seems harmless at first as he owned a lumber business, but gradually reveals a darker side as Enoch becomes increasingly isolated and consumed by his obsession. His life revolves around acquiring and caring for these planks of wood, leading to strange and unsettling behaviors that hint at deeper psychological issues.

Enoch’s secret is that he shut down his lumber business when he fell in love with a dryad. The dryad appeared to him mangled, cut, and disfigured. She was one of the many victims of Enoch’s trade, being turned into timbers and sent across the lands. The slicing, nailing, and bending of the wood planks caused great pain and torture to the dryads, but it never killed their spirits outright. Only fire would set them free, and so Enoch began tracking down chests, cabinets, nightstands, and all the like in order to tear them apart to planks. Using wire and glue he remade trees plank by plank, then burned them to set the dryads free.

You can read the full story here.

This adventure adapts the story with an opportunity for PCs to loot the mansion, finish Enoch’s work, and earn the Oath of the Dryads.

Background

Panic grips the streets as news spreads that Enoch Warren, the notorious "Lord of Mad Mansion," was caught stealing an antique cherry makeup vanity from a local museum. Once a respected lumber magnate, Enoch became a recluse, obsessed with collecting and burning furniture. His madness was largely dismissed until he was spotted carrying a severed arm—believed to belong to a missing girl—as he fled the scene.

Wounded but not caught, Enoch returned to his mansion with the vanity in tow. An angry mob plans to ransack the mansion, and dig up the grounds to find the girl. The museum curator offers the PCs a reward of 750 gp to recover the vanity before the mob destroys the heirloom. (This reward is heavily suggested to be donated back to the museum, and secretly cannot be paid)

Location Details

The mansion windows have had their wooden shutters torn off and are sealed with iron plates from the inside. The adventure begins at nightfall. There is no light unless otherwise noted. Ceilings are 10 ft unless noted. Unsafe.

Rumors

@UUID[RollTable.37pq2gpxTiaASw3h]{Lord of Mad Mansion Rumors}

d6

Rumor

1

He’s been burning all the furniture in that mansion. Every last bit! (P)

2

Enoch used to be a great painter, and had an art studio in his tower. (T)

3

The ghost of his ex-wife cursed him! That’s why he’s gone mad. (P)

4

I heard that one of the antiques he acquired cursed the heck out of him. (F)

5

There’s treasure hidden in the mansion, something beyond gold or jewels. (T)

6

I heard he gets barrels of glue sent to the mansion for the giant rats. (P)


Random Encounters

@UUID[RollTable.AvTBHiEAb8h5Djwa]{Lord of Mad Mansion Random Encounters}

d4

Encounter

1

@UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.LFx9hb8JlEfGxDaI]{Mimic}: A mimic reveals itself and attacks with surprise.

2

Living Plank: A plank of wood, animated by a trapped dryad spirit, skitters across the floor. It attempts to fly into random PCs' arms. DC 12 DEX or be hit in the chin and knocked out cold. Can be awoken next round.

3

Dryad’s Lament: A mangled dryad spirit appears, mournfully singing a haunting tune. Her song has a magical effect: all PCs must make a DC 12 WIS or be lulled into a trance, becoming immobilized for 1d4 rounds unless they take damage or are shaken awake by another PC.

4

Haunting Whisper: The voice of a female calls out, “Help me… free me…” It echoes from the great hall in Area 7, coming from one of the trees.

After the fourth random encounter, the angry mob arrives in [[/r 1d4+2]] rounds. Announce this to players. 10 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.BviPIbrJao1ubOX1]{knights} and 20 @UUID[Compendium.shadowdark.monsters.Actor.V75YwrR126oziTKk]{peasants}, split between @UUID[.YXroFHUvMwfYcShZ]{Area 1} & @UUID[.GKW5jkpj1fzWG8u1]{Area 2}.

Large iron door, set of stairs rise 7 ft up. A large pile of ash sits by the door. Torn up and charred books are scattered about the burnt-up lawn.

Ash Pile: 1.5 ft of white ash topped with still smoldering coals. Prodding reveals wire mesh. The ashes smell faintly chemical. Carelessly disturbing or moving through the coals - 1d4 dmg.

Iron Door: Locked. Past-due bills and collections notices glued to the door. Thieves’ tools or DC 18 STR to open.

The foundations of what used to be a large porch. Big holes where posts were removed. Older remnants of ash and fire. Scattered planks lie tangled in chicken wire. Poorly glued sheets of tin serve as a door. Door is elevated 7 ft from the ground. Two-story tower rises 60 ft.

Door: PCs need a boost or grappling hook. Makeshift door to Area 3 is unlocked.

Holes: 12 1 ft sq deep holes. Can be covered with planks, ash, and dirt to make pit traps. Boobytrap with spikes and caltrops.

Window: An open window on the northwest side of the tower can be spotted, leading to Area 13. DC 18 DEX to climb without a grappling hook.

A 10 ft ladder lies on the floor to @UUID[.GKW5jkpj1fzWG8u1]{Area 2}. A few tall bookshelves stand tall and empty. There are a number of catalogs and papers scattered about. Paper stacks cover a metal table.

Table: Numerous furniture catalogs and Enoch’s notes. They indicate that he has spent considerable time trying to purchase the cherry vanity but was denied. He writes “fine, I’ll steal it so I can make you whole again”. A family tree shows dozens of names, most crossed off. Three names circled at the top – Arethne, Melne, Chryseis. Arethne has a heart by the name.

Stone floor caked with bark and wood scraps. Destroyed husks of furniture fill the hall. Enoch Warren can be seen in @UUID[.TlWL8MHj85bqdOOa]{Area 5} resting on the vanity. He has an arrow in his back, a lit lantern on the vanity.

Enoch: Gravely wounded and sobbing. When alerted, addresses PCs with faint breath and begins dousing himself with oil. Attempts to convey his innocence and urges them to finish his mission. “Please, set the last three free, I haven’t been able to finish. Burn me with Arethne…destroy the last things I care for, for them”. Enoch will try to burn himself and the vanity together, but stumbles with his lantern and only lights himself ablaze.

Debris: Broken furniture and bark scraps, move half speed or [[request 9 DEX]] and risk slipping.

Doors: Door to the north is blocked by wire spools. Door to the south is unlocked.

Enoch’s burning corpse is next to the cherry vanity, which is badly damaged. A single plank of cherry wood is laid on top of the vanity; it is not from the vanity itself. A dying lantern provides light within near. Moldy couches and tapestries of forests.

Cherry Plank: When a PC interacts with the plank or vanity, the cherry plank temporarily morphs into a woman’s arm, and it points the PCs down the hall to @UUID[.QDtWNbb83FxeJtkW]{Area 7}. It lightly pulls PCs holding it towards the tree to be attached.

Cherry Makeup Vanity: Destroyed into planks with attacks or crowbar.

Stairs: To @UUID[.MRDwjKaMTlDVaI48]{Area 12}. Inspecting railing determines wood banister was torn off the iron.

Women’s restroom to the north, men’s to the south. Both have sinks, and a floor-to-ceiling mirror.

Women’s Restroom: Pristine and perfumed. Sponge on stick hangs on the wall next to an ornate peacock sink of stone. Three perfume vials on the sink ledge. Fancy tub holds a pile of clean towels.

Men’s Restroom: Filthy shower. Torn book pages and bills beside the toilet. Ornate stone bull sink. Bull has a nose ring – if tugged, mirror opens to @UUID[.zS4J5SZwWG8PnpMW]{Area 11}.

Perfume: Charm, 1 use. Your Charisma stat becomes 18 (+4) for [[/r 1d6]] rounds.

20ft ceilings. Smells sweet and sticky. Three partially made wire cylinders rise in alcoves across the hall, the westernmost having some branches of bent, pliable wire mesh. Blankets and pillows are found in the raised northern portion of the hall. Three 10 ft ladders by each metal base. Along the middle, remnants of a long banquet table and chairs.

Makeshift Bed: Key to @UUID[.zS4J5SZwWG8PnpMW]{Area 11}. Love letters to Arethne – Enoch documents his finances drying up as he struggles to acquire the last pieces of furniture holding the sister spirits of Arethne. He laments he must soon turn to theft.

Puzzle: Tree names - Arethne (cherry vanity, west), Melne (pine table, north), Chryseis (maple armoire, east). If PCs inspect the partially made trees, they can determine what type of wood is needed for completion. Trees need wood scraps from the correct furniture piece, wire for the frame, and glue to hold it together. It takes 1 round to assemble wire mesh into the trunk shape, and 1 round to glue planks to the mesh to form a tree. Arethne is the most complete and tree-like, needing glue and a few cherry planks from the cherry vanity. Melne and Chryseis have trunks complete but need branches - wire, glue, and their remaining wood scraps. Melne requires the pine pool table. Chryseis requires the maple armoire.

The PC that lights a tree on fire feels a kiss on their cheek. If the three trees are assembled and burned, the dryad spirits of Arethne, Melne, and Chryseis appear before the PCs and bestow the Oath of the Dryads. The whole mansion can be lit ablaze, but to get the Oath players must complete all three trees.

In disarray, pots and pans are strewn about and the smell of burnt wood lingers in the air. A few cabinets remain, but almost all other wood containers have been destroyed. A butcher’s table covered in rust.

Intact Cabinets: Searching reveals 6 days of rations, 22gp3sp, and two jeweled silver goblets (3 gp).

Butcher’s Table: A cleaver is chipped and hacked, with a few metal buckets under the table. The buckets contain random rusted bits of metal, cut into bits. Metal bits can be used as rust monster bait. If used with a vial, can be thrown.

Door: Unlocked, but a sticky substance (glue) is leaking under the door from @UUID[.vvSeyZeQQ5iuYC4v]{Area 9}.

Secret Door: Cabinet with one cookbook (switch). Scratch marks on the floor. Outside, piles of rusting nails, hinges, and other odd bits.

Piles of planks, stacks of old destroyed furniture, and dozens of metal glue barrels.

Rust Monsters: Three @UUID[Actor.UpLhKe3BD9u53K9o]{rust monsters} wait in surprise, hiding between furniture and barrel stacks. Careful observation from outside the room can spot eaten barrels spilling glue, nullifying surprise.

Glue Barrels: Heavy to carry, but can be rolled.

Three large spools of wire block the south door. A beautiful tapestry of a forest scene hangs on the west wall, featuring Enoch and his wife. Other paintings and mosaics also feature the couple. West door is locked. Ornate wood and iron door with a porthole looks into @UUID[.zS4J5SZwWG8PnpMW]{Area 11}.

Wire Spools: Large, blocking doors. Can be rolled to @UUID[.QDtWNbb83FxeJtkW]{Area 7}. Wire mesh is used for building the tree frames.

Paintings: Many paintings of the nude Mrs. Enoch, signed by Enoch.

Swords: Four +1 silver short swords are hung on the wall decoratively.

Frescos depicting gladiatorial combat. Beneath the frescos are two large red velvet sofas, a bar table with furniture catalogs, and a doll. In the middle of the room is a large pool table, with pool cues crossed on top. Smells like smoke and yeast.

Door: Locked. Thieves’ tools or [[request 18 STR]] to open.

Bar Table: Walnut wood. Furniture catalog reveals the pool table was crafted out of lumber from Enoch’s mills. @UUID[Item.KqxPRZ3LyekzVDaS]{Dryad nesting dolls} sit on top of the table next to blocks of chalk. Empty tankards stink of stale ale.

Pine Pool Table: Destroyed into planks with attacks or crowbar. Table is large, best smashed up here.

Warm tapestries and quilts fill a small sitting room, leading to a comfy untouched bedroom. There is a large armoire, chests, and smaller lockers and boxes around. From a regal bed covered with a veil, a faint voice can be heard asking for Enoch.

Hickory Chest: Contains the Owlbear Costume.

Maple Armoire: Large, best broken up in the room to move planks. Destroyed with attacks or crowbar. Shatters if shoved down the stairs and alerts @UUID[Actor.kGRn9d1BPbqeWFcw]{Mrs. Warren}. [[request 18 STR]] to move the armoire safely down the stairs.

Ghost of Mrs. Warren: Corporeal. Appears as she was when she was dying of cancer years ago, before Enoch’s madness. She wears a loose white silk robe (20gp). She mistakes a PC for Enoch, and wishes to spend time with him. She asks him to send his company home, and to head upstairs with her for alone time. If refused, becomes incorporeal and attacks. Attacks if she sees PCs looting or hears them destroying her furniture. If the armoire is broken loudly while @UUID[Actor.kGRn9d1BPbqeWFcw]{Mrs. Warren} is upstairs, she will leave the PC she is with and seek out the disturbance.

Mrs. Warren brings one PC to the top of the tower, into the Northwest studio room. The top tower rooms are filled with easels, brushes, rolls of blank canvas, and dozens of jars of paint. One room is stacked with crates of fake wood fruit and dried flowers.

Paint Me Like One of Your French Girls: Mrs. Warren wants to be painted in the nude. She drops her towel and lays down on a couch, telling Enoch to paint her one last time before she dies. The moonlight from the open window turns her appearance from sickly and frail, to young and beautiful. She has little patience if the PC delays, and expects a painting in 3 rounds. Art supplies are abundant and the PC can ask the young Mrs. Warren to be creative. Three consecutive [[request 12 CHA]] checks are needed to complete the painting with favor, otherwise she is hostile.

Mrs. Warren can be seduced by charisma or song. Bards have advantage on all actions with Mrs. Warren. A single [[request 18 CHA]] check can be attempted to seduce the ghost and abandon the painting task, occupying the PC for 2 rounds. If failed - hostile. If at any point Mrs. Warren turns hostile because of actions below, she ignores the PC with her. Otherwise, she possesses the PC and returns to the group with surprise.

@UUID[Item.9McDRLGr8TfwP7nA]{Owlbear Costume }(250 gp): Exceedingly life-like costume, real feathers. Probably from a masquerade. Two parts, the headdress and the body. Two people are needed to operate the body, while one person wears the headdress. Intelligent humanoids LV6 and below DC 18 WIS or DC 21 WIS with surprise, flee in terror. Uses 1 inventory slot for each person wearing the costume, 3 if carried. Very flammable.

@UUID[Item.KqxPRZ3LyekzVDaS]{Dryad Nesting Dolls}: A set of 7 ivory nesting dolls (120 gp). The innermost one contains a @UUID[Item.U5BtTsKnwGYRwama]{Bead of Force} (SD 299).

@UUID[Item.0JkU3nhSypWmxke7]{Oath of the Dryads}: If the PCs assist in freeing the dryads' spirits, they gain the Oath of the Dryads. When resting in forested areas, Interruption checks are made at DC 9 CON and the danger is reduced by 1 step. If a hostile encounter interrupts rest, PCs may call upon the dryads for aid. Roll 1d6 for number of dryads; on a 6, a treant arrives to help.
